title: Top 10 Goals of the World Cup 2026 Group Stage
summary: From thunderous long-range strikes to intricate team goals, we rank the ten finest goals scored during the group stage of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
content:
The group stage of the 2026 World Cup produced 98 goals across 48 matches, but some efforts stood head and shoulders above the rest. Here are the ten best strikes that lit up the opening phase of the tournament.

10-8: Power and Precision

At number ten, Rodri's dipping volley from 30 yards against Costa Rica showcased the Manchester City man's technique in Spain's 3-0 victory. Ninth place goes to Vinicius Jr's mazy solo run against Serbia, beating four defenders before finishing with aplomb in a vintage Brazilian display. Federico Valverde takes eighth spot with a rasping drive from distance that crashed in off the crossbar during Uruguay's opening match, a goal that exemplified his extraordinary striking ability.

7-5: Moments of Magic

Seventh place belongs to Bukayo Saka's curling effort against Denmark, a carbon copy of his memorable Euro 2024 strike that bent into the far corner with unerring accuracy. At six, Phil Foden's delicate chip over the advancing goalkeeper against Iran demonstrated the kind of audacious skill that defines World Cup memories. Number five is Lamine Yamal's breathtaking strike from the edge of the box against Japan, the 18-year-old announcing himself on the biggest stage with a goal of rare quality and composure.

4-2: Spectacular Strikes

Fourth goes to Florian Wirtz for his free kick against Japan that swerved and dipped over the wall with mathematical precision. Takefusa Kubo claims third with his incredible individual goal against Germany, picking up the ball in his own half and gliding past three challenges before slotting home. Second place belongs to Hakim Ziyech's magnificent curling strike against Uruguay, a left-footed masterpiece that nestled in the top corner.

1: Goal of the Group Stage

The best goal of the group stage belongs to Kylian Mbappe. The French captain collected the ball 35 yards from goal against Australia, shifted onto his right foot, and unleashed an unstoppable strike that flew into the net at over 115 kilometers per hour. The sheer power, technique, and audacity of the effort made it an instant World Cup classic and a reminder of Mbappe's extraordinary ability to produce magic on the grandest occasions.
